# package link

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/link"
```

Package link implements the link transmission procedures of IEC 60870-5-2 over FT 1.2 frames (package ft12): the control field, unbalanced transmission with a [Primary](#type-primary) (controlling) station polling one or more [Secondary](#type-secondary) (controlled) stations, and [Balanced](#type-balanced) transmission between two combined stations.

It is shared by IEC 60870-5-101, -102 and -103. Those companion standards restrict the procedures (which function codes, address sizes, single character use); the restrictions are configured by the caller through [Config](#type-config), not built in.

The procedures implemented (IEC 60870-5-2 clause 4):

  - S1 send/no reply: [Primary.SendNoReply](#func-primary-sendnoreply), used for broadcast
  - S2 send/confirm: [Primary.SendConfirm](#func-primary-sendconfirm), [Primary.ResetLink](#func-primary-resetlink), [Primary.ResetUser](#func-primary-resetuser), [Balanced.Send](#func-balanced-send), [Balanced.Test](#func-balanced-test)
  - S3 request/respond: [Primary.RequestStatus](#func-primary-requeststatus), [Primary.RequestData](#func-primary-requestdata)

with the frame count bit (FCB/FCV) protocol: a primary toggles FCB for every new message with FCV set and repeats a message with the same FCB after a time-out; a secondary that receives a repeated FCB resends its previous response without processing the message again. With one bit, a repetition that arrives after the next message cannot be told from a new message (TestRepetitionAfterTheNextMessage).

A primary that receives only responses that cannot answer its message (a late answer to an earlier one, a wrong function code) until the last time-out returns an error wrapping both ErrUnexpected and ErrTimeout, so a caller that re-initializes the link after ErrTimeout does so in that case too.

[Config.FrameGap](#func-config-framegap) (default [Config.Timeout](#func-config-timeout), negative disables) discards an unfinished frame when the line stays idle longer than that inside it (IEC 60870-5-1 6.2.4.2, rules R2 and R4), using [ft12.Decoder.Gap](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-iec60870-5/ft12#Decoder.Gap).

## Variables

```go
var (
	// ErrClosed reports an operation on a closed station.
	ErrClosed = errors.New("link: closed")
	// ErrTimeout reports that the secondary did not answer within
	// Config.Timeout after Config.Retries repetitions.
	ErrTimeout = errors.New("link: no response")
	// ErrNack reports a secondary that answered NACK (function code 1):
	// the message was not accepted, the link is busy.
	ErrNack = errors.New("link: message not accepted (NACK)")
	// ErrNotFunctioning reports function code 14: link service not
	// functioning.
	ErrNotFunctioning = errors.New("link: link service not functioning")
	// ErrNotImplemented reports function code 15: link service not
	// implemented.
	ErrNotImplemented = errors.New("link: link service not implemented")
	// ErrUnexpected reports a response that does not answer the request:
	// a wrong function code or the address of another station. When only
	// such responses came until the last time-out, the error also wraps
	// [ErrTimeout]: the secondary did not answer the message.
	ErrUnexpected = errors.New("link: unexpected response")
	// ErrInvalidConfig reports a Config a station cannot be built with.
	ErrInvalidConfig = errors.New("link: invalid configuration")
	// ErrDataFlow reports a secondary with DFC set: it cannot accept
	// further user data now, and did not clear DFC while the primary
	// requested the status of link (IEC 60870-5-101:2003 6.2.1, figures 5
	// and 8).
	ErrDataFlow = errors.New("link: data flow control (DFC) set")
	// ErrNoData reports user data without octets: a frame without an ASDU
	// is a fixed-length frame (IEC 60870-5-101:2003 6.1), so send/confirm
	// and send/no reply of user data need at least one octet.
	ErrNoData = errors.New("link: empty user data")
)
```

Errors. They are wrapped with detail; test with errors.Is.

## Types

### type Balanced

```go
type Balanced struct {

	// last FCB sent
	// the peer's last response had DFC set

	// secondary state

}
```

Balanced is a combined station of balanced transmission: it is primary for the messages it initiates and secondary for its peer's. Both directions run at the same time over a full-duplex line.

Its secondary answers only request status of link and reset of remote link until the peer reset the link (IEC 60870-5-101:2003 figure 9). Its primary waits for the peer to clear DFC before it sends user data again (figure 8).

#### func NewBalanced

```go
func NewBalanced(rw io.ReadWriter, cfg Config, bc BalancedConfig, h BalancedHandler) (*Balanced, error)
```

NewBalanced starts a balanced station on rw. Close stops it; rw is closed when it is an io.Closer.

#### func (Balanced) Close

```go
func (b *Balanced) Close() error
```

Close stops the station and waits for its goroutines. It closes rw when rw is an io.Closer; the reader goroutine returns only when that Close unblocks Read, so a transport whose Close does not leaves Close waiting. Close is safe to call more than once and from several goroutines: the first call closes the transport and returns its error; later calls return nil.

A handler must not call Close: Close waits for the reader goroutine that runs the handler. Call it in a new goroutine (go b.Close()); it returns once the handler has returned.


Done is closed when the station stops.


#### func (Balanced) Init

```go

```

Init brings up this station's direction of the link: request status of link until the peer answers with DFC = 0, then reset of remote link (IEC 60870-5-101:2003 figure 8). See [Primary.Init](#func-primary-init) for the repetition.

#### func (Balanced) RequestStatus


RequestStatus sends request status of link and awaits status of link.

#### func (Balanced) ResetLink

```go
func (b *Balanced) ResetLink(ctx context.Context) error
```

ResetLink sends reset of remote link; the next FCV message carries FCB = 1.

#### func (Balanced) Send

```go
func (b *Balanced) Send(ctx context.Context, data []byte) error
```

Send sends user data with confirmation. When the peer's last response had DFC set it first requests status of link until DFC is clear ("secondary link busy", IEC 60870-5-101:2003 figure 8) and fails with ErrDataFlow when it stays set. Empty data fails with ErrNoData.

The frame refers to data without copying it: data must not be modified after the call, since a frame queued before ctx ended is still sent. When ctx ends during the exchange the frame count bit of the message is spent although no confirmation came: if the message did not reach the peer, the peer takes the next message with the same user data for a repetition of the last one it accepted and does not deliver it. Run an exchange that must not lose its message under a context that outlives it, as the iec101 client does.

#### func (Balanced) Test

```go
func (b *Balanced) Test(ctx context.Context) error
```

Test sends the test function for link and awaits the ACK.

### type BalancedConfig

```go
type BalancedConfig struct {
	// Addr is this station's link address: the peer's primary messages
	// carry it, and this station's responses too. With a 0-octet address
	// field it is ignored.
	Addr uint16
	// Remote is the peer's link address, carried by this station's
	// primary messages.
	Remote uint16
	// DIR is the direction bit of every frame this station sends:
	// IEC 60870-5-2 sets it in frames from station A (by convention the
	// controlling station) and clears it in frames from station B.
	DIR bool
}
```

BalancedConfig identifies the two ends of a balanced link.

### type BalancedHandler

```go
type BalancedHandler interface {
	// UserData delivers user data from the peer. Returning false refuses
	// it: the station answers NACK with DFC set.
	UserData(data []byte) bool
	// Reset is called for reset of remote link (user false) and reset of
	// user process (user true) from the peer.
	Reset(user bool)
}
```

BalancedHandler is the user of a balanced station: it receives the peer's user data. Calls come from the station's reader goroutine, one at a time, and must return quickly. They run with the station's secondary state locked, so the handler must not call Close, which waits for that goroutine: call it in a new goroutine (go b.Close()), which returns once the handler has returned. The handler may call Send and the other primary methods only from another goroutine: their answers arrive on the goroutine the handler blocks. The data passed to UserData is a copy the handler may keep; the station also keeps it to recognise a repetition, so it must not be modified.

### type Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// FT12 holds the address field size.
	FT12 ft12.Params

	// Timeout is how long a primary waits for the response to a message
	// before it repeats it. Zero means [DefaultTimeout]. It must exceed the
	// round trip plus the transmission time of the longest frame
	// (IEC 60870-5-101:2003 6.2.2, formulas (1) and (2)): about 2.25 s at
	// 1200 bit/s with 240-octet frames. The 1 s default suits 9600 bit/s
	// and faster, and transports such as TCP.
	Timeout time.Duration

	// Retries is how often a primary repeats a message that was not
	// answered. Zero means [DefaultRetries]; negative means none.
	Retries int

	// SingleCharAck makes a secondary answer with the single character
	// E5h instead of a fixed-length ACK, and instead of a fixed-length
	// "no data" NACK when neither ACD nor DFC is set (IEC 60870-5-2 5.1).
	// Primaries always accept E5h.
	SingleCharAck bool

	// SenderAddr makes a balanced station's responses (secondary
	// messages) carry its own link address instead of the peer's. By
	// default they carry the address of the receiver, the peer:
	// IEC 60870-5-101:2003 6.2.1.2 asks for the receiver's address "in
	// primary and secondary messages". lib60870-C v2.4.1 answers with its
	// own address and accepts either. Responses with either address are
	// accepted whatever this says. Unbalanced stations ignore it.
	SenderAddr bool

	// FrameGap is how long the line may stay idle inside a frame: octets
	// of a frame whose next octet comes later are discarded as a frame
	// that never ended (IEC 60870-5-1 6.2.4.2, rules R2 and R4, which
	// leave no idle interval between the characters of a frame). Without
	// it a start character in line noise, or a peer that stopped in the
	// middle of a frame, makes the station take the octets of the next
	// frames as the rest of that one: with L = 255 the next 261 octets.
	// Zero means Timeout; negative disables the check. Over a transport
	// that splits frames with pauses (a terminal server on a congested
	// network) choose it above the longest pause.
	FrameGap time.Duration

	// OnFrame, when set, is called for every frame sent (tx true) and
	// received. It runs on the station's goroutines and must not block
	// or call Close, which waits for those goroutines. f.Data of a sent
	// frame is the caller's data, of a received one the copy the
	// station delivers: neither may be modified.
	OnFrame func(tx bool, f ft12.Frame)

	// OnDiscard, when set, is called for octets that do not form a
	// valid frame (line noise, checksum errors). It runs on the
	// station's reader goroutine and must not call Close. b is the
	// decoder's buffer, valid only during the call: copy what is kept.
	OnDiscard func(b []byte, err error)
}
```

Config holds the link parameters.

### type FCBResetHandler

```go
type FCBResetHandler interface {
	ResetFCB()
}
```

FCBResetHandler is implemented by a [SecondaryHandler](#type-secondaryhandler) that serves function 7 "reset of frame count bit", the IEC 60870-5-103 extension (6.3): ResetFCB is called after the station reset its expected FCB and before it answers ACK. Function 7 is not a function of IEC 60870-5-101 (table 3): a secondary whose handler does not implement this interface answers it with function 15 "link service not implemented".

### type FlowControlHandler

```go
type FlowControlHandler interface {
	Busy() bool
}
```

FlowControlHandler is implemented by a [SecondaryHandler](#type-secondaryhandler) or a [BalancedHandler](#type-balancedhandler) that reports data flow control: while Busy returns true every response carries DFC = 1 (IEC 60870-5-2 5.1; IEC 60870-5-103 6.3), and user data with confirmation (function 3) is answered NACK with DFC = 1 without being delivered ("secondary link busy", IEC 60870-5-101:2003 figures 6 and 9).

### type FunctionFilter

```go
type FunctionFilter interface {
	Implemented(fn byte) bool
}
```

FunctionFilter is implemented by a [SecondaryHandler](#type-secondaryhandler) that restricts the primary function codes it serves, as a companion standard does (IEC 60870-5-103 6.2.3): a message with a function code for which Implemented returns false is answered with function 15 "link service not implemented" and not processed (IEC 60870-5-103 6.3). The FCB bookkeeping is the same as for an accepted message.

### type Primary

```go
type Primary struct {

	// last FCB sent per secondary

}
```

Primary is the primary station of unbalanced transmission: it is the only station that initiates messages, and polls the secondaries addressed by link address. Methods are safe for concurrent use; the exchanges are serialized because the line carries one at a time.

The frames refer to the caller's user data without copying it: data passed to SendConfirm or SendNoReply must not be modified after the call. SendNoReply returns once the frame is queued, and a frame queued before the context of SendConfirm ended is still sent. The user data RequestData returns is the caller's.

When the context of SendConfirm ends during the exchange the frame count bit of the message is spent although no confirmation came: if the message did not reach the peer, the peer takes the next message with the same user data for a repetition of the last one it accepted and does not deliver it. Run an exchange that must not lose its message under a context that outlives it, as the iec101 client does.

#### func (Primary) Init

```go
func (pr *Primary) Init(ctx context.Context, addr uint16) (Status, error)
```

Init brings up the link to a secondary: request status of link until it answers with DFC = 0, then reset of remote link (IEC 60870-5-2 5.1, link initialization; IEC 60870-5-101:2003 6.2.1.1, figure 5). While the secondary answers with DFC = 1 the request is repeated every Config.Timeout, at most Config.Retries times, then Init fails with ErrDataFlow.

#### func (Primary) RequestData

```go
func (pr *Primary) RequestData(ctx context.Context, addr uint16, c Class) ([]byte, Status, error)
```

RequestData polls a secondary for user data of class c (function 10 or 11). It returns the user data, or nil when the secondary has none (function 9 or E5h), with the secondary's status: ACD set means class 1 data is waiting.

#### func (Primary) RequestStatus

```go
func (pr *Primary) RequestStatus(ctx context.Context, addr uint16) (Status, error)
```

RequestStatus sends "request status of link" (function 9) and returns the status of link the secondary answers with (function 11).

```go
func (pr *Primary) ResetFCB(ctx context.Context, addr uint16) (Status, error)
```

ResetFCB sends function 7 "reset of frame count bit", the IEC 60870-5-103 extension (6.3). Like ResetLink, the next message with FCV set carries FCB = 1.

#### func (Primary) ResetLink

```go
func (pr *Primary) ResetLink(ctx context.Context, addr uint16) (Status, error)
```

ResetLink sends "reset of remote link" (function 0). On success the next message with FCV set carries FCB = 1.

#### func (Primary) ResetUser

```go
func (pr *Primary) ResetUser(ctx context.Context, addr uint16) (Status, error)
```

ResetUser sends "reset of user process" (function 1).

#### func (Primary) SendConfirm

```go
func (pr *Primary) SendConfirm(ctx context.Context, addr uint16, data []byte) (Status, error)
```

SendConfirm sends user data with confirmation (function 3). It returns ErrNack when the secondary did not accept it, and ErrNoData for empty data, which has no variable-length frame (IEC 60870-5-101:2003 6.1).

#### func (Primary) SendNoReply

```go
func (pr *Primary) SendNoReply(addr uint16, data []byte) error
```

SendNoReply sends user data without reply (function 4), typically to the broadcast address. Nothing is awaited. Empty data fails with ErrNoData.

### type Secondary

```go
type Secondary struct {

	// the primary reset the link since the station started

}
```

Secondary is the secondary station of unbalanced transmission: it answers the messages addressed to it and ignores the others. Until the primary resets the link (function 0) it answers only request status of link and reset of remote link and ignores every other message (IEC 60870-5-101:2003 6.2.1.1, figure 6).

Close is safe to call more than once and from several goroutines: the first call closes the transport and returns its error; later calls return nil.

A handler must not call Close: Close waits for the reader goroutine that runs the handler. Call it in a new goroutine (go s.Close()); it returns once the handler has returned.

### type SecondaryHandler

```go
type SecondaryHandler interface {
	// UserData delivers user data from the primary (function 3, or
	// function 4 when broadcast or no reply is expected). Returning false
	// refuses it: the station answers NACK with DFC set.
	UserData(data []byte, broadcast bool) bool

	// Class1 returns the next class 1 user data, or nil.
	Class1() []byte
	// Class2 returns the next class 2 user data, or nil.
	Class2() []byte
	// HasClass1 reports whether class 1 data is waiting (ACD).
	HasClass1() bool

	// Reset is called for reset of remote link (user false) and reset of
	// user process (user true).
	Reset(user bool)
}
```

SecondaryHandler is the user of a secondary station: it receives the primary's user data and supplies the data the primary polls. Calls come from the station's reader goroutine, one at a time, and must return quickly: the primary is waiting for the response. They run with the station's state locked, so the handler must not call Close, which waits for that goroutine: call it in a new goroutine (go s.Close()), which returns once the handler has returned.

The station keeps what Class1 and Class2 return, to send it again when the primary repeats its request (FCB not toggled): the handler must not modify it afterwards. The data passed to UserData is a copy the handler may keep; the station also keeps it to recognise a repetition, so it must not be modified.
